text:
marta: Heads-up — VoltChip bench kickoff tomorrow 09:00 PT. Primary goals: perf/W curves across p8/p16, baseline throughput at 512/1024 tokens, and a first-pass kernel-tune sweep.

raj: Perfect. Do we have the dataset and prompt-set finalised? I can push the eval set to S3 tonight.

marta: Yes — Cheng merged the eval bundle into s3://redwood-bench/voltchip/dayone. It's light (10k samples) so runs fit into an hour per config.

cheng: Confirmed. Dataset: openqa-llm-v2 subset, and a small promptbank for long-context (1k tok) stress. Also added a kernel flag matrix: 
```
KV_CACHE=true
BATCH=32
QUANT=fp16,4bit
KERNEL_HINT=gemm_fast|attention_fused
```

emily: Thanks. On VoltChip side Ben asked for us to try their power telemetry agent; they'll stream watt readings to our bench agent via the partner webhook. Any objections?

raj: Fine as long as telemetry is tagged and we keep raw traces behind the bench account. Need the mapping between partner sensors and our metrics schema.

marta: Ben (VoltChip) sent the mapping in the onboarding doc. Will upload and link in the run playbook. We'll run two passes: 1) baseline with Redwood runtime default kernels, 2) partner-suggested kernel hints. Compare throughput, 95p latency, and J/s/W.

bench-bot: Job scheduled: voltchip-dayone-baseline on gpu-pool-a, id=vc-20250301-01. ETA 09:02 PT. Logs -> https://bench.redwood.internal/jobs/vc-20250301-01/logs

cheng: Quick checklist for tomorrow:
- confirm VoltChip telemetry handshake (Ben)
- ensure GPU power sampling at 500ms windows
- run short smoke on one shard (5m)
- upload kernel hint configs to /configs/voltchip/dayone/

marta: I'll coordinate with Ben on the handshake at 08:30. @raj can you own uploading the comparison script that calculates W_per_token and normalised throughput? I want the final CSV to have columns: config, model, batch, seq_len, tokens/s, watts_avg, tokens_per_watt, 95p_latency_ms.

raj: On it. I'll also add a note to strip GPU fan noise periods from watt aggregation.

emily: VoltChip asked whether we want them to push a custom kernel build or just provide tuning flags. I recommended flags first to keep validation simple. If flags look promising we can try the build next sprint.

marta: Agreed. Keep the build as opt-in. We want reproducible runs for the marketplace listing.

bench-bot: Smoke run complete: vc-20250301-01 — PASS. Baseline throughput 1.8k tokens/s at batch=32 seq=512, avg_watts=420W. Full logs available.

cheng: Nice. Early signal looks sane. Save the smoke artifacts under artifacts/voltchip/dayone/smoke-20250301.tgz

marta: Plan for public-facing comms: if the partner wants a co-announcement we need final, reproducible numbers and a short methods appendix (bench env, model versions, kernel flags). We'll draft a 1-pager after the full sweep.

raj: Timeline: sweep completes by EOD tomorrow, initial analysis by Friday. I'll open the PR for the comparison script now.

emily: I'll ping Ben post-sweep to ask about readiness for a joint blog outline.

marta: Thanks team. Quick notes: keep raw telemetry internal; only publish aggregated tokens_per_watt and throughput curves. Any blockers — drop them here or DM. :thumbsup:
